# LoopMovie <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Movies](BlitzBasic-Movies)

</div>


```blitzbasic
LoopMovie:Void movie:Int32, loop:Int32=1
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `movie` | In | Int32 | required | A movie handle from [OpenMovie](OpenMovie). |
| `loop` | In | Int32 | `1` | 1 to loop the movie, 0 to play it once. The default is 1. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Makes a movie begin again at its start when it reaches its end, so that [MoviePlaying](MoviePlaying) stays 1 until looping is turned off, or the movie is closed. Turn it off with `LoopMovie movie, False`: the movie then plays to the end it is at and stops. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals can only play a movie once. The sound of the end is played to its last sample before the movie begins again, so there is a short pause in the sound between the rounds.

## Differences

* A debug build (`-d`) stops the program when the movie does not exist, for example the 0 of a movie that failed to open, other builds ignore the command, see [Debug handle checks](Debug-Handle-Checks).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
movie = OpenMovie("background.mpg")
LoopMovie movie
While Not KeyHit(1)
	DrawMovie movie, 0, 0
	Flip
Wend
```
